findings.text: First dirtying of a clean folio updates mapping state and propagates dirtiness to the owning inode and reports success, while marking an already dirty folio reports no change without further accounting.
Locked dirtying holds the folio lock across the dirty transition and returns the outcome of that transition to the caller.
Redirtying after an incomplete write counts skipped pages for the current pass and reverses prior dirtied accounting when the mapping supports writeback.
Dirty cancellation adjusts writeback accounting when the mapping supports writeback and otherwise clears the dirty indication without accounting.

Mapping dirty tagging applies only when the folio remains associated at lock time, tolerating concurrent truncation by leaving tags unchanged when detached. Swap cache and shared memory associations are programming errors, and dirtying a folio whose contents are not current can warn when requested.

Folios move among clean, dirty and under writeback conditions with tag state tracking each condition. Beginning writeback records inode level activity on first entry and reconciles dirty and to write tags with current flags. Ending writeback clears the writeback tag, advances completion accounting, releases inode activity when no tagged pages remain, and schedules a delayed bandwidth refresh.
Dirty and writeback tag mutations are serialized by the mapping page tree lock held with interrupt state saved, covering both direct updates and extended cursor updates.
Writeback waiting blocks until the writeback indication clears with a wait trace each cycle, and abandons waiting with an interrupt status when the killable sleep is interrupted.
Stable waiting delays for writeback completion only for mappings that require stable pages during writeback and otherwise returns immediately.
Writeback initiation is valid only for a locked folio not already under writeback and requires successful accessibility preparation, with violations treated as fatal folio state errors.
Writeback completion maintains pending and completed write counters and reports whether waiters were present when the writeback indication cleared.
Dirty marking tolerates detachment racing with truncation, and writeback waiting rechecks the writeback condition after each wake because completion and reentry can interleave.
Lookup within a free area returns the first free buddy of the requested mobility kind or absence when that list is empty.

Splitting a larger free block preserves total free capacity except for pages converted to guards, installs correct orders on resulting buddies, places remainders on appropriate free lists, and charges only pages handed out.

Allocation is satisfied from the lowest order at or above the request that holds the desired mobility, with larger blocks reduced to the requested size. Absence is reported when no suitable block exists in any larger order.

Preferred mobility misses fall back in fixed order with unmovable preferring reclaimable before movable, movable preferring reclaimable before unmovable, and reclaimable preferring unmovable before movable.

Large requests take ownership of an entire block directly with type conversion. Smaller requests convert a foreign block only when enough pages within it are free or compatible and otherwise fail without conversion. Unsuccessful direct attempts can raise reclaim pressure and mark the zone boosted when background reclaim participation is allowed.

Watermark boosting grows by one pageblock up to a capped maximum derived from the high watermark and a boost factor, and is declined for tiny zones, disabled boosting, or uninitialized high watermarks.
Freshly allocated pages are validated against expected flag state before use, with checks extended across the whole block when checking is enabled and unexpected state routed to bad page handling.

New pages receive post allocation accounting, compound initialization for multi page compound allocations, and pfmemalloc marking exactly when watermark checks were bypassed with the mark cleared otherwise.
Transfers between pending and batch deferred free queues and their counters are serialized by a per processor spin lock held with interrupts disabled.

Per processor deferred free state comprises a serialization lock, a pending queue, a batch queue awaiting grace completion, a pending count, a deferred reclamation work item, and an expedite work item.

Deferred freeing preserves per zone accounting by applying counter updates at zone boundaries and at the end, tolerates arbitrarily large batches by yielding the processor, and counts total pages and completions.

Early initialization creates a reclaim capable per processor workqueue for deferred freeing and prepares empty queues and work items on every possible processor, with the queue pointer immutable after init.

Deferred pages wait in a pending set, move to a batch set after grace handling, and then become free. An expedited drain can consume the pending set directly after an expedited grace wait when the regular path has not already taken it, with empty drains treated as no operation.

Only skip type standalone bits are valid for per block queries, with each operation resolving the owning bitmap word and offset before testing or updating a single bit. Invalid selections warn and leave state unchanged.
Iteration over deferred batches captures the successor before freeing because freeing reuses linkage storage, and zone accounting is deferred until pages are actually freed.
Hardware poisoned pages bypass generic bad page reporting on allocation, with buddy marking cleared when present to avoid spurious complaints about known bad pages.
Free page internal control is a bitwise integer where none equals zero, skip report notify is bit zero, to tail is bit one, no lock is bit two, and prepared is bit three.
Deferred free expedite threshold equals one thousand twenty four and minimum per processor high fraction equals eight.
Allocation stall warning interval equals ten thousand milliseconds with the last warning timestamp initialized to the initial jiffies value.
Zone display names in index order are DMA then DMA32 then Normal then HighMem then Movable then Device, with DMA variants and HighMem and Device conditional on build options.
Mobility display names in order are Unmovable then Movable then Reclaimable then HighAtomic then CMA then Isolate, with the last two conditional on build options.
Low memory reserve ratios default to two hundred fifty six for DMA and DMA32, thirty two for Normal, and zero for HighMem and Movable.

Minimum free memory defaults to one thousand twenty four kilobytes with user override default negative one. Boost factor defaults to fifteen thousand, scale factor to ten, and defragmentation mode defaults to zero.

Possible nodes default to all and online defaults to node zero alone, with non NUMA normal memory and processor sets defaulting to node zero and high memory similarly when present. Allowed mask starts as the boot mask, pageblock order is read mostly, identifier count starts at maximum with one online node, movable zone index starts at zero, mobility grouping disable starts cleared, and deferred pages key starts enabled.
Per processor local node, kernel local memory node and NUMA statistics key provide topology and accounting state. Latent entropy storage is volatile with entropy attribute.
One build delegates deferred zone growth to the growth helper and reports its result while the other build always reports no growth.
One build serves contiguous fallback from the smallest suitable CMA block while the other build always reports absence for such fallback.
One build pins the current task by disabling preemption with matching re enable while the other pins by disabling migration with matching re enable.
One build updates zone counters directly with caller preserved context while the other preserves interrupt state across the update.
Tag clearing releases any attached code tag reference by emptying it and updating the handle before dropping the handle, with absence of a reference leaving state unchanged.
Per processor batch high updates and per processor draining are each serialized by a dedicated mutex.
